declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated over two rounds. Class counsel’s opening proposal was $30 million for the class, distributed automatically, and $9 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses; it also included a clear-sailing provision, with any fee amount not awarded added to the class fund. Brightline countered with $25 million for the class and $6 million in fees and expenses, automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees added to the class fund. Class counsel then proposed $27 million for the class and $7 million in fees and expenses, retaining automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and the provision that any unawarded fees be added to the class fund. Brightline accepted that proposal as binding, subject to court approval. Fees were discussed in the opening round alongside the proposed class relief; they were not discussed only after class relief had been agreed. The settlement provides $27 million for approximately 400,000 identifiable class members, with payments sent automatically and no claims process. The proposed fee is subject to independent court review, Brightline has not agreed not to oppose the fee request, and any amount the court does not award will benefit the class. The settlement provides substantial and prompt relief while avoiding the risks, delay, and expense of further litigation, including the risks of class certification and trial. In light of those considerations, class counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate, subject to the Court’s independent review under Rule 23(e).
